prompt: Complete a SupplyCrate inventory whose add and remove methods defend three invariants: no zero-count entries, never more units than the capacity, and a rejected call must change nothing.
explanation: Checking every precondition before touching the map is what makes a rejected call a true no-op -- once you start mutating halfway through a validation you can no longer back out. Reading the current count through a helper that turns a missing key into 0 removes the null handling from every call site. Deleting the key when a count reaches zero keeps the invariant that a name is present only while the crate really holds some of it, which is what makes itemNames trustworthy.
hints: Write countOf first: items.get(name) returns null when the key is absent, so turn that into 0 before anything else uses it.
Do all the validation up front in add and remove, and only then call items.put -- that is how a rejected call leaves the crate untouched.
In remove, compare the requested quantity with the current count: equal means items.remove(name), less means put the reduced count back. Sort a new ArrayList of the key set for itemNames.
